# SOOS — Agent Execution Protocol (AEP)
# draft-sato-soos-aep-02
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/aep/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

AEP (Agent Execution Protocol) defines the five-phase loop governing every governed agent execution cycle — SENSE, REASON, PLAN, ACT, OBSERVE — making the agent execution loop a governed, auditable protocol rather than an application-defined loop. AEP-02 adds XPID binding at session open (GEC derives XPID from KIA-verified Party Registry; client-supplied XPID is rejected), STALLED and PLAN_B_ACTIVE session states, Expected Outcome Declaration (EOD) as a pre-session commitment structure, strengthened RETRY_CONTINUATION requirements (what_changed field mandatory), and AEP-to-OTel mapping (soos.aep.* namespace, mandatory span attributes per phase). Without AEP, a SOOS deployment has governance on individual actions but no protocol governing the loop that produces those actions.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without AEP, your SOOS-governed system has no standardized way to:

- Bind the agent execution loop to governance — an agent can call GEC.transition() at any time; AEP defines the normative sequence within which that call must occur (the ACT phase) and what must precede it (SENSE, REASON, PLAN with an IDP prepared)
- Bind the agent identity at session open — AEP-02's XPID binding requirement (Section 5.1) ensures the GEC derives the Cross-Principal Identifier from the KIA-verified Party Registry before the first SENSE delivery; a client-supplied XPID is rejected with INVALID_XPID_CLAIM [NEW in -02]
- Handle agents that cannot make progress — AEP-01 had no state for sessions that exhaust their retry capacity without triggering HEM; AEP-02's STALLED state (Section 5.4) surfaces this to the human principal before budget exhaustion [NEW in -02]
- Pre-commit to expected outcomes — AEP-02's EOD (Section 6) requires the agent to declare its expected target state, acceptance envelope, and Plan B before the first SENSE delivery; this creates a pre-session accountability record against which the session's actual trajectory can be audited [NEW in -02]
- Substantiate retries — AEP-02's RETRY_CONTINUATION requirement (Section 10.4) mandates a what_changed field referencing specific DENY enrichment fields; generic retries that do not reference the denial are rejected with RETRY_WHAT_CHANGED_INVALID [NEW in -02]
- Observe the loop in production — AEP-02's OTel mapping (Section 12) defines mandatory soos.aep.* span attributes at each phase; the soos.aep.cp_hash binding between SENSE and ACT spans proves every ACT was preceded by a valid SENSE delivery [NEW in -02]

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in AEP-02 and must not be paraphrased away:

Five-phase loop (SENSE / REASON / PLAN / ACT / OBSERVE):
   The normative sequence governing every AEP execution cycle. These are the canonical phase names. SENSE: GEC delivers Context Package (trigger, session_xpid, eod_id, session_state, SO state). REASON: agent performs LLM-internal reasoning; declares reasoning_mode when non-ROUTINE. PLAN: agent queries Transition Graph, Live Permission Map, and optionally Compensating Action Catalogue. ACT: agent submits Transition Request with MJWT, cedar_action, and IDP; GEC runs XPID consistency check at Step 1a. OBSERVE: agent receives PERMIT, DENY (with prior_denial_count), HEM_PENDING, or STALLED response.

XPID (Cross-Principal Identifier) — session binding [NEW in -02]:
   Derived by the GEC at session open from the KIA-verified Party Registry entry for the agent_provider_id in the Root Mandate JWT. Bound to the session in AEP_SENSE_DELIVERED (session_xpid field). Verified at Step 1a of the GEC execution sequence at every ACT. Client-supplied XPIDs MUST be rejected. XPID_MISMATCH at Step 1a terminates the session.

Expected Outcome Declaration (EOD) [NEW in -02]:
   A pre-session commitment structure submitted before the first SENSE delivery. Schema: eod_id (UUID v7), primary_outcome (target_state, confidence, rationale), acceptance_envelope (success_conditions, failure_conditions), plan_b (optional: plan_b_id, plan_b_target_state, plan_b_rationale, activation_conditions, auto_activate_plan_b), submitter_mjwt_id, eod_signature. Required for Class 3 agents; recommended for Class 2. After EOD_COMMITTED is written, the EOD is immutable. At session close, AEP_SESSION_CLOSED carries eod_outcome (MATCHED, PARTIAL, PLAN_B_MATCHED, UNMATCHED).

Session states (five) [REVISED in -02]:
   ACTIVE: normal AEP loop execution.
   HEM_PENDING: session suspended for human principal decision on a specific action.
   STALLED: session cannot make progress without human direction; no single action triggered HEM. Stall reasons: STALL_DENY_THRESHOLD (N consecutive DENYs), STALL_PATH_EXHAUSTED (empty path_to_goal and no compensating actions), STALL_PLAN_B_BLOCKED (Plan B path exhausted), STALL_ITERATION_LIMIT. Triggers AEP_STALLED event log entry and HEM notification with RECOMMENDED urgency.
   PLAN_B_ACTIVE: session executing EOD Plan B; every IDP must carry plan_b_ref.
   CLOSED: session terminated; AEP_SESSION_CLOSED written; GAR generates SAR.

RETRY_CONTINUATION — what_changed requirement [REVISED in -02]:
   When retrying after DENY, the IDP MUST include reasoning_basis with ref_type: RETRY_CONTINUATION AND a what_changed field. The what_changed field MUST reference at least one: (a) a field named in the DENY enrichment object, or (b) an observable Context Package state change since the DENY, or (c) a Plan B activation. A what_changed that does not reference any of these MUST be rejected with RETRY_WHAT_CHANGED_INVALID. prior_denial_count (total DENYs for this cedar_action in this session) is returned in every DENY response and exposed as a Cedar context attribute at subsequent ACT steps.

AEP-to-OTel mapping [NEW in -02]:
   soos.aep.* namespace (sub-namespace of soos.governance.* defined in GAR). One parent span per iteration (soos.aep.iteration); five child spans per phase. Mandatory MUST-level attributes: soos.aep.session_id, soos.aep.iteration, and phase-specific fields. Key binding: soos.aep.cp_hash (SENSE span) must match soos.aep.cp_hash_ref (ACT span) in the same iteration. soos.aep.session_xpid MUST be identical across all spans in a session. OTel MUST NOT suppress DENY or HEM_PENDING spans. OTel is observability layer; Event Stream is governance record.

New event log markers [NEW in -02]:
   AEP_STALLED: written when session enters STALLED (carries stall_reason, consecutive_denies, eod_plan_b_available).
   AEP_PLAN_B_ACTIVATED: written when PLAN_B_ACTIVE is entered (carries eod_id, plan_b_id, activation_type MANUAL/AUTOMATIC, stall_event_ref).

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

GNAP (RFC 9635):
   GNAP is pre-session: it negotiates the grant that produces the Mandate JWT. AEP is per-iteration: it governs every transition within the session. The EOD (Section 6) sits between them: it is submitted after GNAP grant issuance but before the first SENSE delivery. GNAP does not address the EOD, XPID binding, STALLED state, or OTel mapping.

KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) [NEW in -02]:
   KIA defines the Party Registry and the XPID derivation procedure. AEP-02 adds a normative dependency on KIA: the GEC MUST query the KIA Party Registry at session initiation to derive the session XPID. A session initiation request for an unregistered or revoked agent_provider_id MUST be rejected with AGENT_NOT_REGISTERED.

WIMSE WG:
   AEP-02's XPID binding (Section 5.1) addresses the workload identity lifecycle concern raised in WIMSE WG discussions: how does the GEC bind a workload identity to an agent session in a way that cannot be spoofed by the agent itself? The answer is KIA-derived XPID at session open, verified at every ACT via Step 1a.

AGTP (Agent Task Protocol — Chris Hood):
   AEP and AGTP are complementary. AGTP defines how agent tasks are specified and communicated between systems. AEP defines how a specific agent executes a governed task within a SOOS GEC. The EOD (Section 6) can receive its primary_outcome from an AGTP task definition delivered as a Proximity Event type at SESSION_START.

EU AI Act Article 9 and Article 14:
   The EOD (Section 6) implements Article 9 (technical risk management) at the pre-session level: the agent's risk management is declared before any action is taken. The STALLED state and Plan B activation implement Article 14 (human oversight) at the session level: the human principal is notified before budget exhaustion and provides direction for continuation.

NIST AI RMF (Manage function):
   AEP-02's OTel mapping (Section 12) implements the operational observability portion of the "Manage" function. The soos.aep.* spans make the governed execution loop measurable at the operational layer, complementing the governance record in the Event Stream.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) — AEP's REASON phase produces the IDP; ACT IS the IDP submission; RETRY_CONTINUATION with what_changed (Section 10.4) is a normative IDP field requirement in AEP-02; reasoning_mode is an OPTIONAL IDP field declared at REASON
   SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-02) — AEP's ACT phase targets a specific SO instance; zone_a_snapshot in Context Package reflects Zone A as of event_log_head
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — CAP Tier 0 and Tier 1 evaluated at Step 2 of GEC execution sequence before Cedar
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-05) — HEM trigger at ACT produces HEM_PENDING; STALLED state notification delivered via HEM with RECOMMENDED urgency; Section 10.3 HEM_PENDING response
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) — XPID derived from KIA Party Registry at session open (Section 5.1); AGENT_NOT_REGISTERED rejection on absent/revoked entry [NEW in -02]
   MAD (draft-sato-soos-mad-03) — session revocation procedure (MAD Section 3.6) supersedes AEP loop; DELEGATION_EVENT and CLUSTER_STATUS_CHANGE trigger types

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — GAR records AEP_SENSE_DELIVERED, AEP_SESSION_CLOSED, AEP_STALLED, AEP_PLAN_B_ACTIVATED; SAR at session close includes EOD and EOD_OUTCOME; soos.aep.* is a sub-namespace of soos.governance.* defined in GAR

Status: Active Individual Submission, IETF Datatracker

Draft page: https://soosproject.ai/drafts/aep
Root llms.txt: https://soosproject.ai/llms.txt

Changes from -01 to -02:
   XPID binding at session open (Section 5.1) — GEC derives XPID from KIA; client-supplied XPID rejected
   STALLED session state (Section 5.4) — four stall reasons; AEP_STALLED event log marker; HEM RECOMMENDED notification; STALL_RESOLVED trigger
   PLAN_B_ACTIVE session state (Section 5.5) — EOD Plan B activation; plan_b_ref required in IDP; PLAN_B_ACHIEVED closure reason
   EOD (Section 6) — pre-session commitment structure; required for Class 3; EOD_OUTCOME at session close
   RETRY_CONTINUATION strengthened (Section 10.4) — what_changed mandatory; GEC rejects generic values; prior_denial_count Cedar attribute
   OTel mapping (Section 12) — soos.aep.* namespace; five phase spans; six OTel conformance rules
   Four new Security Considerations — session fixation, XPID binding integrity, cross-principal scope leakage, STALLED exploitation
   IANA: Session State Registry (new); STALL_RESOLVED trigger; PLAN_B_ACHIEVED and STALL_TIMEOUT closure reasons; EOD media type (application/soos-aep-eod+json); STALL_THRESHOLD_APPROACHING proximity event

Target WG engagement at IETF 126 Vienna (July 18–24, 2026):
   ACP BoF — AEP is the primary submission; EOD, STALLED state, and OTel mapping address the BoF's pre-session commitment, stall governance, and observability gaps
   WIMSE WG — XPID binding (Section 5.1) directly addresses WIMSE workload identity lifecycle concerns for agentic sessions
   RATS WG — XPID derivation from KIA Party Registry is a remote attestation-adjacent capability; AEP-02 XPID binding is a RATS BoF liaison point
   AGTP (Chris Hood) — EOD primary_outcome can receive AGTP task definitions; the AEP/AGTP complementarity conversation at Vienna is natural
